headline: A T. rex skeleton sells for 50 million dollars

sources.title: Mystery bidder buys T. rex nicknamed 'Gus' for a record $50 million
T. rex sells for $50 million, becoming the most expensive dinosaur fossil ever auctioned
Rare T. rex fossil sells for record $50.1 million at auction
T. rex skeleton Gus sells for a record $50.1 million (video, Reuters)

chunks.text: A skeleton of a Tyrannosaurus rex sold for 50.1 million dollars in New York on July 14. The [[auction house]] had expected it to {{go for}} 20 to 30 million, so the price almost [[doubled]] the highest [[estimate]]. The buyer [[bid]] by telephone and has not been named. No dinosaur has ever sold for more. The old [[record]] was almost 45 million dollars, paid for a stegosaurus in 2024. The sale has {{stirred up}} an old argument about who should be allowed to own a [[fossil]] like this.

verbs.correct: To be sold for a price
verbs.why: Go for means to sell for a certain price at an auction or a sale. The auction house expected the T. rex skeleton to go for 20 to 30 million dollars.

verbs.wrong: To bring an old argument to an end
verbs.why: Stir up means to bring old, strong feelings back to the surface again. The record sale has stirred up an old argument about who should own rare fossils.

chunks.text: The skeleton is [[nicknamed]] Gus. It is about 67 million years old, 38 feet long and 12.5 feet tall. A team {{dug up}} the bones on a [[ranch]] in South Dakota in 2021. [[Freeing]] them from the rock and then {{cleaning up}} every piece took five years. The ranch belonged to a farmer called Gary Licking, and he died before that work was finished. The team chose the nickname in his [[memory]].

verbs.why: Dig up means to remove something buried, usually with careful, slow work. A team dug up the T. rex bones on a ranch in South Dakota in 2021.
Clean up here means to carefully remove rock and dirt from each fossil bone. Freeing the skeleton from the rock and cleaning up every piece took the team five years.

chunks.text: About 61 percent of Gus is real bone, which is a lot for a T. rex. Most skeletons in museums are [[largely]] [[plaster]]. The [[skull]] is almost [[undamaged]]. Gus also kept its [[furcula]], a thin V shaped bone across the chest that we call the wishbone in a chicken. That bone is [[fragile]] and it very rarely {{shows up}} in a fossil this old. Those three things together are why the bidding {{shot up}}.

verbs.wrong: To be listed in a book
verbs.why: Show up means to appear or be present, here inside a very old fossil. The delicate wishbone bone very rarely shows up in a fossil this old and this complete.
Shoot up means to rise very quickly and by a large amount. Because the skeleton was so rare and complete, the bidding shot up fast during the auction.

chunks.text: Scientists were less pleased than the sellers. The incoming president of a society of fossil experts said she hoped the buyer would {{hand over}} the skeleton to a museum. Once a fossil is {{locked away}} in a private house, researchers cannot [[measure]] it, and no public museum can {{keep up with}} private [[bidders]] at these prices. The buyer has not {{come forward}}. So the most complete Tyrannosaurus to [[reach the market]] in years now [[belongs to]] an owner whose name nobody knows, and the people who wanted to study it have been {{shut out}}.

verbs.wrong: To sell it at a discount
verbs.why: Hand over means to give something you own to another person or group. The expert hoped the anonymous buyer would hand over the skeleton to a public museum.

verbs.wrong: To sell without a public auction
verbs.why: Lock away means to keep something shut inside a place others cannot enter. Once a fossil is locked away in a private house, researchers cannot study it at all.
Keep up with means to match the pace or the spending of someone else. No public museum can keep up with private bidders paying record prices at auction.
Come forward means to reveal yourself publicly after staying hidden or anonymous. The buyer of the T. rex has not come forward, so nobody knows their name.

verbs.wrong: To be asked to pay for access
verbs.why: Shut out means to deliberately keep someone from being included or having access. The researchers who wanted to study the skeleton have now been shut out completely.

mainIdea.s: A Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton sold for just over 50 million dollars, almost double the top estimate. Scientists worry the fossil will now sit in a private home where researchers cannot study it.
mainIdea.why: The auction house had expected 20 to 30 million dollars, and the buyer has not been named. A fossil expert hoped the buyer would hand the skeleton over to a museum instead.

mainIdea.s: The fossil sold for such a high price partly because it kept a rare wishbone bone, rarely found. The buyer then came forward and promised the skeleton would go straight to a public museum.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the buyer never came forward. The article says the buyer bid by phone and has stayed unnamed, which is exactly what worries fossil experts.

mainIdea.s: A stegosaurus skeleton sold for almost 45 million dollars in an earlier sale, which set the old record. Museums later raised money and tried to buy similar fossils for public display.
mainIdea.why: This is about the earlier stegosaurus sale, not the T rex sold in 2026. The stegosaurus sale is only mentioned as the old record that this new sale broke.
